title: SQL Injection Detection, Triage, and Remediation Playbook
source: OWASP Top 10:2021 A03 (Injection) & NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 (SI-10)
content:
### 1. OVERVIEW & DETECTION
SQL Injection (SQLi) occurs when untrusted user input is directly concatenated into dynamic database queries without parameterized validation, allowing attackers to manipulate database commands. Threat variants include in-band (UNION-based, error-based), blind (boolean-based, time-based with sleep()/WAITFOR DELAY), and out-of-band SQLi. Detection indicators include:
- Web Application Firewall (WAF) rule violations matching SQL meta-characters and syntax (e.g., ' OR 1=1--, UNION SELECT, ; DROP TABLE, admin'#).
- Database syntax error messages reflected in HTTP 500 responses or server error logs (e.g., ORA-01756, You have an error in your SQL syntax, Unclosed quotation mark).
- Anomalous spikes in HTTP request latency caused by time-based blind SQLi payloads (e.g., pg_sleep(10), BENCHMARK(5000000,MD5(1))).
- Unusually large HTTP response payloads indicating bulk data extraction from database tables.

### 2. EVIDENCE & ARTIFACTS TO EXAMINE
- WAF & Reverse Proxy Logs: Examine request URIs, query parameters, POST request bodies, User-Agent strings, and client IPs for SQL injection signatures.
- Web Application Access & Error Logs: Review HTTP status codes (especially 500 Internal Server Error vs 200 OK) and response byte sizes.
- Database Audit Logs: Query logs from MySQL, PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, or Oracle examining syntax errors, unauthorized schema queries (information_schema, sys.tables), and elevated stored procedure executions (e.g., xp_cmdshell, pg_read_file).
- Database Connection Strings & Privileges: Inspect database user permissions to determine if the web tier connects under administrative/sa/root privileges.

### 3. INVESTIGATION & TRIAGE
- Determine Exploit Success: Verify whether the injection payload successfully extracted sensitive records, altered database contents, or failed safely due to input handling.
- Assess Impact Scope: Check if the affected database contains Personally Identifiable Information (PII), authentication credentials, payment data, or trade secrets.
- Inspect Stored Procedures & System Calls: If Microsoft SQL Server or PostgreSQL is used, determine whether OS-level command execution (xp_cmdshell) was attempted or enabled.

### 4. CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES
- WAF Rule Enforcement: Implement or tighten WAF blocking rules for the vulnerable URI endpoint and block attacking source IPs at the perimeter.
- Temporary Endpoint Disablement: If the vulnerability is critical and being actively exploited, temporarily disable or restrict access to the specific API route pending code patching.
- Database Account Lockdown: Revoke elevated administrative privileges from the application database service account immediately.

### 5. ERADICATION, RECOVERY & REMEDIATION
- Mandate Parameterized Queries: Refactor all dynamic SQL statements to use prepared statements / parameterized queries across all database access layers (or use an Object-Relational Mapper / ORM safely).
- Principle of Least Privilege: Ensure web application database accounts possess only SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE rights on necessary tables; revoke DROP, ALTER, and administrative stored procedure permissions.
- Suppress Detailed Error Messages: Disable verbose database error messages in production web responses; return generic error identifiers and log details internally.
- Security Testing & Code Review: Perform Static Application Security Testing (SAST) and Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST) across all API endpoints before re-enabling public access.
